title: UFC 3-340-02: quasi-static gas pressure of TNT in a closed room
summary: TNT fired at the centre of a closed, rigid 6 m cube (216 m^3), 0.25 to 4 kg/m^3: the steady gas pressure left once the shocks die down, against UFC 3-340-02's design curve (Figure 2-152). At light charges most of it comes from the products burning in the room's oxygen.

notes: The case does not prescribe when to read the pressure: report it once the shock reverberations have decayed (in a 6 m room, tens of milliseconds) and say when, and whether the products burn (afterburning) and lose heat.
UFC 3-340-02 calls Figure 2-152 a curve fitted to tests of partly vented chambers with A/V^(2/3) up to 0.022 and gives no scatter; the tests themselves are not in hand.
Heavy charges (2-4 kg/m^3) have too little oxygen to burn all their products, so the curve flattens.
